name: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd.
business_summary: The passenger-vehicle entity after the Tata Motors demerger: Jaguar Land Rover (about two-thirds of revenue, Range Rover/Defender/Discovery at 81% of wholesales) and the Indian PV and EV business (Nexon, Punch, Harrier, Curvv; ~14.3% share in Q1 FY27, targeting 15% soon and 20% by FY31; EV mix 20-23% of sales). Consolidated TTM revenue Rs 3.44 lakh cr but EBITDA margin only 4.9%, so earnings are highly geared to JLR volumes, commodities, FX and US tariffs. Net debt ~Rs 42,000 cr at Q1 FY27.

revenue_mix.geography: UK ~25% of wholesale, North America, Europe, China <8%, rest of world

cost_structure.note: India EV battery content as % of India revenue, model estimate

exposures.mechanism: JLR bodies are aluminium-intensive; aluminium ~4% of consolidated sales (model estimate). +10% -> 0.4% of sales = ~Rs 1,370 cr vs TTM EBITDA Rs 16,910 cr -> -8% pre pass-through; ~25% recovered -> -6%; EV/MCap ~1.4 (net debt ~Rs 42,000 cr), persistence 0.4 -> -3.4. Very high operating leverage: TTM EBITDA margin only 4.9%. Aluminium -19.6% since June is a tailwind.

evidence.note: Consolidated EBIT margin 2.4%, JLR EBIT 2.8%, net debt Rs 42,000 cr
Aluminium -19.6% since 2026-06-01

exposures.mechanism: Steel ~4% of consolidated sales (JLR and Tata India; model estimate). +10% global HRC -> 0.4% of sales = Rs 1,375 cr -> -8% of EBITDA pre; ~30% recovered -> -5.7%; x1.4 x0.4 = -3.2, rounded -3.0. Global HRC is +20.6% since June (factor_state): large headwind. Company said commodity pressure would persist in Q2.

evidence.note: TMPV expects commodity pressure to persist in September quarter; needs to accelerate cost reduction
Global HRC +20.6% since 2026-06-01

exposures.mechanism: Copper ~1.5% of sales (harness, motors, EV). +10% -> Rs 515 cr -> -3% EBITDA pre; 30% recovered -> -2.1%; x1.4 x0.4 = -1.2.

evidence.note: Elevated commodity prices cited in Q1 domestic PV margin pressure

exposures.mechanism: EVs ~20-23% of India volumes (34,000+ units in Q1, 20% mix, exit 23%) plus JLR EVs. India revenue ~Rs 72k cr/yr x 20% x battery ~35% = ~Rs 5,000 cr battery content; +15% cell cost -> +10.5% = Rs 525 cr = -3.1% EBITDA pre; 50% recovered -> -1.6%; x1.4 x0.4 = -0.9. PLI accruals (Rs 313 cr in Q1) partly offset.

evidence.note: EV volumes >34,000 in Q1 FY27, ~20% mix, exit 23%; PLI accrual Rs 313 cr

exposures.mechanism: Direct oil-linked inputs (plastics, paints, freight) ~6% of sales; +10% Brent -> 0.15% of sales net -> -3% EBITDA pre... x1.4 x0.4 -> -1.0, plus JLR Middle East demand disruption ('market disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East', Q1 FY27) ~-0.2. Pack empirical -0.53 per +10% (t -0.6) is insignificant. Offsetting EV demand benefit is on a separate substitution edge.

evidence.note: JLR Q1 volumes impacted by market disruption linked to conflict in the Middle East

exposures.mechanism: Higher fuel prices pull India demand toward EVs where Tata has ~60%+ of the market (model knowledge): TMPV said EV volumes +112% y/y 'supported by demand growth following the West Asia conflict'. +10% Brent -> EV mix +1pp (20% -> 21%) -> EV unit margin gap + PLI -> EBITDA +2.5% x1.4 x0.3 = +1.0. Note this is a parallel path to the input-cost Brent edge; Director should net them (net ~-0.2).

evidence.note: EV volumes +112% y/y supported by demand growth following the West Asia conflict

exposures.mechanism: JLR (about two-thirds of revenue and most of EBITDA, ~Rs 12k cr) reports in GBP/translated to INR: a weaker INR vs GBP lifts reported INR earnings. +3% -> +3% on ~Rs 12k cr = +Rs 360 cr = +2.1% EBITDA; JLR is also net long USD/CNY revenues vs GBP/EUR costs; India business imports ~10% of cost partly offsets. Net +1.5-2.5 x1.4... = +2.0. Pack empirical +2.78 per +3% (t +1.2) consistent. Note: Q1 FY27 adverse FX hit the domestic business.

evidence.note: Empirical USDINR +2.78 per +3% (t +1.2)
Elevated commodity and FX costs hurt domestic PV business

exposures.mechanism: North America is JLR's largest-profit region and the strategic refocus (June investor day). +1pp US demand growth -> JLR US volume +1.5% -> JLR EBITDA +5.6% (contribution ~30% vs EBITDA margin ~8%); JLR ~70% of group EBITDA -> +3.9%; x1.4 x0.5 = +2.7 -> 2.5.

evidence.note: June investor day: double-digit revenue growth target, refocus on North America

exposures.mechanism: UK is JLR's biggest wholesale region (21,000 units in Q2 FY27, 25% of 82,400) and Europe ~20%. +1pp UK/Europe demand growth -> JLR volume +1.2% -> EBITDA +4.5% x0.7 group share x1.4 x0.5 = +2.2 -> 2.0. UK is preparing duties on Chinese EVs (Times of London 2026-10-05) - mild positive for JLR share.

evidence.note: JLR Q2 wholesales 82,400 (+24.5%); UK 21,000; China 6,100 (-46%); UK Chinese-EV tariff plan

exposures.mechanism: China wholesales fell 46% to 6,100 units in Q2 FY27 after local production ended in June; the market is now <8% of JLR volume. +1pp China growth -> +0.3% JLR volume ... -> +0.6. Chinese-brand competition in UK/EU is a separate risk.

evidence.note: JLR China wholesales -46% to 6,100 in Q2 FY27

exposures.mechanism: US ~25% of JLR revenue (~GBP 6bn/yr). A +10pp additional US tariff on UK/EU-built autos = GBP 600m; if half absorbed = GBP 300m = Rs 3,500 cr = 21% of TTM EBITDA; x1.4 x0.5 persistence... -> -10 to -14 if unmitigated; with mitigation (price, mix, US assembly via Stellantis MoU) central -8. Current status unverified in this session; shown as conditional risk edge. Proposed new node.

evidence.note: JLR/Stellantis MoU on US-specific Defender products; US refocus

exposures.mechanism: India PV business is ~20% of revenue and ~17% of EBITDA but a larger share of growth value; +25bp -> India PV volume -0.4% x gearing 4 (EBITDA margin only ~4%) -> -1.6% India EBITDA = -0.3% group; plus multiple compression on a high-beta (1.4) stock ~-0.3 = -0.5. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07.

evidence.note: Repo +25bp to 5.50%

exposures.mechanism: India business: Q1 revenue Rs 18,000 cr (+65%), EBITDA margin ~4%, volumes ~182,000 (+46%), share 14.3%. +10% industry volumes -> +10% TMPV India volume; contribution ~18% vs 4% EBITDA margin -> gearing 4.5x -> India EBITDA +45% = +7.7% group; x1.4 x0.3 = +3.2 -> 3.0. Oct 2026 industry >5 lakh units; management expects industry +10% for FY27.

evidence.note: India revenue Rs 18,000 cr (+65%), EBITDA margin ~4%, market share 14.3%
Industry growth expected >10% in FY27

exposures.mechanism: Market leader in Indian EVs (EV mix ~20-23%, 70% EV volume growth targeted for FY27). Stronger EV push (+1) -> EV mix +4-5pp, PLI accruals up (Rs 313 cr in Q1 = 5% of quarterly EBITDA) -> EBITDA +4% x1.4 x0.5 structural = +2.8 -> 2.5.

PLI accrual Rs 313 cr in Q1

evidence.note: PLI accrual Rs 313 cr in Q1 FY27

exposures.mechanism: India PV ~20% of revenue; GST 2.0 already boosted volumes (+46% in Q1). A further cut (+1) -> India volume +3% x gearing 4.5 = +13% India EBITDA = +2.3% group x1.4 x0.5 = +1.6 -> 1.5.

evidence.note: India volumes +46% y/y in Q1 FY27

exposures.mechanism: JLR was hit by a component-supplier fire in Q1 FY27 and earlier supply disruptions; +1 SSU = a chip-type shortage cutting JLR output ~5% for a quarter -> JLR EBITDA -18%/quarter = -3% annualised x1.4 ... -3.
